NO WRITES, AS BEFORE: the tool runs under halt_telemetry's isolation (imported, not copied): memo off, temporary CAS and ledger, a copy of data/ for reference reads; a subprocess test hash-compares the stores it is pointed at; a verifier timeout is re-measured once, never retried until it passes.

findings: THE ORDER: the rule that places steps which carry a repeated id or name a missing one after the rest is not a topological order, and costs a pass whenever such a step has a dependent. Measured at ab40c5b in a scratch export (memo off, temporary stores, derivation._evaluation_order patched per call): [a, b uses [a, z], c uses b] takes 2 passes as listed, 2 under Kahn's algorithm over the closure's below, and 3 with b moved last as the criterion says (c is visited before b and waits a pass). [a, a, b uses a, c uses b] and [a, b uses [a, z], c binds b] behave the same way (2 / 2 / 3). So THE MEASUREMENT's MORE-passes exit fires on an order built as planned, or the pin for 'a missing reference' fixes a non-topological order as correct. No special case is needed: a reference that resolves to no single carrier is no edge in below (derivation.py:678-679), and a step carrying a repeated id has no dependents. Fix: Kahn's algorithm over below exactly, ties by listed position, with only Kahn's remainder (the steps on or resting on a cycle of below, self-loops included; static, not the trail's unsettled labels, since FALSE_CYCLE's members settle) appended in listed position. In-degree counts distinct predecessors, because below[i] lists j twice when uses repeats an id (above dedupes at :682). Pin [a, b uses [a, z], c uses b] at 2 passes.

THE ORDER, one copy of the rules: there is no edge construction to import. below is built inline in verify_derivation (derivation.py:648-679: the default id s{i}, str() of every id, a bind source taken as ref.partition('.')[0] and appended to uses, then single-carrier resolution), and this run may not change src/. So 'by import where one exists' licenses a copy, and the planned gates cannot tell a wrong copy from a right one. Measured over the 62 fast tier rows at ab40c5b, a copy that forgets bind sources differs from the closure's below on 22 rows. It never needs MORE passes than listed, and responses and verifier calls stay identical. It still understates the saving on 'README document, listed in reverse', 'BIND, listed in reverse' and 'BIND_FALSE_SOURCE, listed in reverse': 3 passes instead of 2, with every exit silent. None of the five pinned shapes has a bind. The honest alternative takes no copy: the patched _evaluation_order runs at :763, after below exists (:679), so it can read the closure's own edges from its caller's frame (sys._getframe(1).f_locals['below'], measured working here) and run Kahn's on them, failing loudly if the name changes. Require that, or a copy with a test that compares it with the frame-read below on every tier row. Add an oracle check from the closure itself: under the topological order every row takes exactly 2 passes, or 1 where nothing moves in pass 1. Measured, 61 of 62 fast rows take 2 and SELF_BIND 1, the cyclic rows included; a dropped edge fails this check. Pin as well a bind whose source is listed after its user, a bind from a repeated id, and a default id that another step uses.

THE MEASUREMENT, verifier calls: the goal expects 'at most one per step either way', but no exit checks it. The only exit is calls that differ, so a wrapper that double-counts the same way under both orders leaves the counts equal and exits 0, and the planted defect as worded proves nothing. Require: count calls at the closure's one entry (derivation.verify_step, looked up at call time inside the thunk at derivation.py:789), per step (the multiset of (domain, spec hash) under each order, since the RECEIPT rows share one spec). Exit nonzero when either order calls more verifiers than there are steps or counts a step more than once, and when the two orders differ. Plant one defect that double-counts under both orders and one under one order only, and show each trips its exit.

THE MEASUREMENT, identity: the goal calls the comparison 'measurement 2's gate, which must hold at 100%'. That gate compares two fields: the whole response minus halt.passes, and what _transfer settles for each step keyed by node['at'] (order_replica's 'evaluation: settled', tools/order_replica.py:53, :144-150). The second was added because checker-24 measured that the response alone misses per-step outcome and originator changes. THE MEASUREMENT compares only the response. Require both, by importing order_replica's _run and _evaluation_fields: _run (:122-140) already patches _evaluation_order for one call with an explicit order and restores it in a finally. Then the patch and the comparison each live once, as halt_telemetry's isolation does. Show the planted _transfer defect caught in the settled field with the response unchanged.

RECORDED, the product line: no rule fixed before the tool runs decides between 'cheaper derivations for reverse-listed callers' and 'no change', and 'cheaper' is a claim nothing measures. Verifier calls, the cost, are identical by construction, so all the saving is in closure passes. The control also reaches the floor. A run whose first pass moves anything takes at least 2 passes under any order, because the pass that moves nothing is counted, and whether the first pass moves anything does not depend on the order. Measured at ab40c5b, under the topological order 61 of the 62 fast rows take 2 passes and SELF_BIND takes 1, the cyclic rows included; the 1,500-step chain is acyclic and should take 2 (not measured here). So the goal's 'control any future ranker would have to beat' cannot be beaten on this population. Require the criterion to fix the rule now, and the record to state: the unit (passes saved; verifier calls unchanged); no time or cost claim unless the tool measures one; how many rows the topological order brings to the floor (so no ranker or model has headroom here); and how much of the total saving is the one deliberately reversed 1,500-step fixture (1,499 passes if it takes 1,501 listed and 2 topological).
